objects.original: An elementary adapted scalar process and one fixed sample path.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. q is the supplied elementary-process record with deterministic strictly increasing times t_0,...,t_n and real coefficient functions q_i. Its value is q.value(t,omega)=sum_{i=0}^{n-1} 1_{t_i<t<=t_{i+1}}*q_i(omega), zero outside the union of these left-open, right-closed intervals.
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; q.value is the literal sum of indicators of (t_i,t_{i+1}] times coefficients.

domains.original: Any nonnegative horizon, strictly increasing finite grid and arbitrary sample.
domains.reconstructed: Omega with measurable space m; filtration on R_+; n in N; q:ElementaryAdaptedProcess(filtration,n); T>=0; omega in Omega. No measure on Omega is present.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; T is unrestricted NNReal and times need not start at zero or end at T.

quantifiers.original: For every process q, horizon T and sample omega.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally Omega,m,filtration,n,q,T,omega. The q record itself includes for every cell i a strongly-measurable coefficient and an existential bound C_i valid for every omega.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; omega is an ordinary theorem binder, not under an a.e. quantifier.

assumptions.original: Stored left-endpoint measurable, pointwise bounded coefficients; no sample measure is needed.
assumptions.reconstructed: The times t_i in R_+ are strictly increasing. Each q_i:Omega->R is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(t_i), and for each i there exists C_i with |q_i(omega)|<=C_i for every omega. There is no stated t_0=0, t_n=T, or T>0 requirement.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; The elementary structure supplies adaptation and bounds; no additional assumptions are introduced.

conclusion.original: Integral q² equals sum of coefficient squares times clipped cell lengths.
conclusion.reconstructed: For every T and omega, integral_0^T q.value(t,omega)^2 dt = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} q_i(omega)^2 * real(min(t_{i+1},T)-min(t_i,T)), where subtraction on the right is performed in R_+ before casting.
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; lintegral_value_sq plus finite ENNReal.toReal conversion gives exactly the clipped-length real formula.

scopes.original: Pointwise identity including partial or empty intersection with the horizon.
scopes.reconstructed: An exact deterministic identity for every sample point, not an almost-everywhere equality. The interval lengths are clipped by T. The value function uses intervals (t_i,t_{i+1}], and vanishes at t_0 and outside their union.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; Nonnegative time subtraction equals ordinary difference here because the clipped grid is monotone.

constant_dependencies.original: Per-cell coefficient bounds are in the record; none occurs in the identity.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The per-cell bound C_i may depend on q and i, but is independent of omega. These bounds do not appear in the identity. No global measure or expectation is involved.
constant_dependencies.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ProgressivePathEnergy.lean:104; Every term is finite; the finite-sum conversion does not require a uniform sample-independent bound beyond the stored data.
